sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *dejar de* + infinitive from B1 Unit 12: it means to stop doing something. In the story of the transitions it says who stopped governing, who lost support and who left office, and *no dejar de* says that something went on.

items.spanish: Los militares dejaron de gobernar, pero conservaron mucho poder.
items.english: The military stopped governing, but kept a lot of power.

items.spanish: Collor dejó de ser presidente en 1992.
Serrano dejó de tener el apoyo del ejército.
items.english: Serrano lost the army's support (stopped having it).

items.spanish: Los partidos no dejaron de discutir las nuevas reglas.
items.english: The parties kept on discussing the new rules.

sections.content: *Dejar de* is always followed by an infinitive: *dejaron de gobernar*. Put *dejar* in the tense you need (*dejó*, *dejaron*, *dejaba*). With *no*, it means to keep on. Do not confuse it with *dejar* + noun: *Pinochet dejó la presidencia* (he left the presidency).
